Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 711 PM EST Thu Nov 12 2026
 

- Air becomes sufficiently cold for lake effect rain/snow activation 
late tonight and Friday morning. 

- Minor slushy snow accumulation is likely across the Thumb, mainly 
near Saginaw Bay and near the Lake Huron shoreline, southward 
toward the I-69 corridor. 

- Rain/snow showers gradually shift offshore Friday night and 
Saturday with little additional snow accumulation.

&&

.AVIATION...

A mix of MVFR to the north and VFR across the south will start this 
TAF period as shower coverage has decreased for now aside from a 
brief period across FNT for the next hour or two. Cold northerly 
flow and increased lift with multiple waves within the broader 
troughing over the region will lead to a robust lake response with 
models pointing to two dominate lake bands starting late tonight and 
through much of tomorrow afternoon. One band develops off of 
southern Lake Huron with the other one off Saginaw Bay. This puts 
FNT and DET with the higher likelihood to be most impacted 
downstream of these two lake bands. It may be cold enough at FNT for 
a more prevailing snow p-type for much of today with DET warm 
enough for more of a mix of rain and snow. Robust lake response will 
also maintain a MVFR ceilings with pockets of IFR conditions possible 
if any heavier lake band manage to reach these terminals. Expecting 
to see potential for scattered rain/snow showers across other 
terminals as well. Shifting lower level winds towards the northwest 
late tomorrow afternoon will begin to direct lake bands east of the 
terminal corridor with some improvement in ceilings possible by 
tomorrow evening. Winds holding out of the north to around 10 knots. 

For DTW... Recent radar trends lean towards a break from 
precipitation to start this TAF period before the main lake effect 
bands fully form later this morning. The more dominant band looks to 
set up closer towards DET. However, pieces of this activity could 
break off and reach DTW. This would be more focused late morning and 
early afternoon. Temperatures would be warm enough to support a rain-
snow mix in this outcome with minimal if any accumulation. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* High for ceilings at or below 5,000 feet through tomorrow 
  afternoon.

* High for p-type as rain through 06z tonight. Medium for rain-snow 
  with any precip after 06z into tomorrow afternoon.

&&
